Small-Hsiao test of IIA

Source: R/iia.R
small_hsiao.Rd

The likelihood-ratio form of the IIA test with a random half-split of the cases (Small and Hsiao 1985). The full model is estimated on both halves, \(\hat\theta_1\) and \(\hat\theta_2\), and combined as \(\hat\theta_{12} = \sqrt{1/2}\,\hat\theta_1 + (1 - \sqrt{1/2})\,\hat\theta_2\); the restricted model (alternative \(d\) dropped) is estimated on the second half, \(\hat\theta_r\), and the statistic is \(-2[\ell_2^r(\hat\theta_{12}) - \ell_2^r(\hat\theta_r)]\) with the second-half restricted log-likelihood \(\ell_2^r\), chi-square on as many degrees of freedom as restricted parameters under IIA. The weights \(\sqrt{1/2}\) and \(1 - \sqrt{1/2}\) are what make the statistic chi-square; the variant that drops them and also estimates the restricted model on both halves (as in some earlier implementations) is twice a chi-square and rejects far too often.

Usage

small_hsiao(object, drop = NULL, splits = 1L, seed = NULL)

Arguments

object

A fitted mnl() model with at least three alternatives. A fit with diverging coefficients (separation) draws a warning: the contrasts then compare estimates that do not exist and can reject spuriously.

drop

Alternatives to drop, one at a time; default all.

splits

Number of independent half-splits (default 1, the test; more describe how the statistic varies across splits, see Details).

seed

Optional seed for the splits; the caller's random-number stream is restored afterwards.

Value

A data frame of class "iia_test" with one row per split and dropped alternative: split, alternative, statistic, df, p.value, and separated (a fit behind that row has diverging coefficients in an equation the statistic uses: the quasi-separation of a half-sample that a rare alternative with binary covariates invites, after which the statistic may reflect the separation rather than IIA; a divergence confined to the dropped alternative's own equation does not mark the row); with splits > 1 the attribute "summary" holds per alternative the median statistic over the splits, median_p (the chi-square p-value of that median, as iia_tests() reports it; descriptive, since the median of split statistics is not chi-square, and with an even number of splits not the median of the split p-values), the share of splits rejecting at 5 percent, and the share of separated splits. boot_pvalue() calibrates the median (see the IIA vignette).

Details

The split is stratified by chosen alternative. Results can depend heavily on the random split: one split may give a large statistic that the next does not. The test is one split chosen before the data are seen: fix seed in advance (small_hsiao(m, seed = )) and report that split. In the package's size study one split held its level (rejection 0.040 to 0.047 at 0.05), while the median over ten splits rejected in none of 300 samples, so the median is not a test at its level. splits > 1 repeats the statistic on independent splits and reports every one together with the median and the share of splits rejecting at the 5 percent level, a description of how much the statistic varies (Long and Freese 2014 recommend inspecting this variability; iia_tests() reports the median over ten splits); boot_pvalue() can calibrate the median. When the pre-specified split's half-sample fits are separated (separated), its statistic reflects the separation rather than IIA: report the row as uninformative, or calibrate it with boot_pvalue(m, small_hsiao, seed = ) and the same seed. A seed chosen after seeing a result is not a test. Dropping the base alternative is handled by re-basing, as in hausman_mcfadden(). The test is not frequency-weight exact: the halves are balanced in cases, not in weight. The cases are taken as independent: a fit's cluster does not enter the statistic. Not for fixed-effects fits.

References

Long, J.S. and Freese, J. (2014). Regression Models for Categorical Dependent Variables Using Stata, 3rd ed. College Station, TX: Stata Press.

Small, K.A. and Hsiao, C. (1985). Multinomial logit specification tests. International Economic Review, 26, 619-627. doi:10.2307/2526707

See also

hausman_mcfadden(), fp_tests(), iia_tests()

Other IIA tests: boot_pvalue(), fp_tests(), hausman_mcfadden(), iia_tests(), nested_lm_test()

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- rmnl(1200, beta = cbind(b = c(0.5, -1, 0.8), c = c(-0.3, 0.6, -0.5), d = c(0.1, 0.3, 0.9)))
m <- mnl(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d)
small_hsiao(m, seed = 1)
#> Small-Hsiao test of IIA (stratified half-split, sqrt(1/2) weighting) 
#>  split alternative statistic df p.value separated
#>      1           a     6.703  6   0.349     FALSE
#>      1           b     3.603  6   0.730     FALSE
#>      1           c     1.479  6   0.961     FALSE
#>      1           d     5.479  6   0.484     FALSE
small_hsiao(m, drop = "c", splits = 5, seed = 1)
#> Small-Hsiao test of IIA (stratified half-split, sqrt(1/2) weighting) 
#>  split alternative statistic df p.value separated
#>      1           c     1.479  6   0.961     FALSE
#>      2           c     6.583  6   0.361     FALSE
#>      3           c     1.779  6   0.939     FALSE
#>      4           c     4.139  6   0.658     FALSE
#>      5           c     6.484  6   0.371     FALSE
#> 
#> Across splits:
#>  alternative median_statistic df median_p share_reject_05 share_separated
#>            c            4.139  6    0.658               0               0
